name: Local Models for Patient Data
title: Local Models for Patient Data
answer: Local models for patient data are AI systems that run on hardware inside a hospital, clinic or research site rather than sending records to an external service. The scope covers diagnostic support, note summarisation, coding, imaging triage and similar tasks where the input is identifiable health information. It sits inside the wider governance and compliance field because the decision to keep inference on site is usually a data protection decision as much as a technical one. This site tracks 1000 medical AI models, a large share of which are candidates for local deployment.

Governance, Compliance and Medical Device Security

sections.body: Local models for patient data are AI systems that run on hardware inside a hospital, clinic or research site rather than sending records to an external service. The scope covers diagnostic support, note summarisation, coding, imaging triage and similar tasks where the input is identifiable health information. It sits inside the wider governance and compliance field because the decision to keep inference on site is usually a data protection decision as much as a technical one. This site tracks 1000 medical AI models, a large share of which are candidates for local deployment.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These systems run on owned or leased compute: a workstation with one or more GPUs, an on premises server, or a small cluster in the hospital data centre. Some sites use a private cloud tenancy or a dedicated appliance supplied by a vendor, which keeps data inside a controlled boundary even if the hardware is not owned outright. Model weights are downloaded once and stored locally, and inference happens without an outbound network call. Storage, backup and the physical security of the machine become part of the clinical risk surface.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work starts with a model that fits the available memory and latency budget, often an open weight model fine tuned or prompted for the clinical task. Teams build a local pipeline: ingestion from the electronic health record, de-identification where full records are not needed, inference, and a review step by a clinician before anything enters the record. Evaluation uses held out local data rather than public benchmarks, because local patient populations differ from the ones models were trained on. Monitoring covers drift, failure modes and the rate at which clinicians override the output.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Keeping data local reduces exposure under rules such as HIPAA and GDPR but does not remove obligations, since the site is now the operator and often the deployer of the model. A vendor supplying a local model may still be a business associate or a processor, and the contract has to say who is responsible for updates, logging and incidents. If the model influences diagnosis or treatment, it can fall under medical device rules, and the site facts note 6 active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, which shows how disputes can reach the vendor and the deploying institution. Provenance of training data, model version and every inference that informed a decision should be recorded so the reasoning can be reconstructed later.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Smaller and more efficient models are making local deployment practical on modest hardware, and this is shifting some clinical AI from central services to the edge of the hospital network. Expect more attention to standardised audit logs, signed model artefacts and clear lines of responsibility between vendor and site. Regulation is still catching up, and the 229 compliance and regulation pages tracked here reflect how quickly that area is moving. The likely direction is hybrid: local inference for identifiable data, with central services reserved for de-identified or aggregate work.
